```{r}
the.seed <- 42
set.seed(the.seed)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)

  library(ggplot2)
  library(readxl)
  library(gprofiler2)

```

```{r}
sample.name <- "brain_DV200"
```

## Which tumour states are present?

Neftel et al. (Cell, 2019) showed that glioblastoma cells are found in 4 main states : **MES-like** (mesenchymal), **AC-like** (astrocyte), **OPC-like** (oligodendrocyte progenitor) and **NPC-like** (neural progenitor). Each state is defined by a gene list (meta-module), MES and NPC are split in two (MES1/MES2, NPC1/NPC2). We score our malignant cells with these lists to see which states dominate this tumour.

The object with the CNV results was reloaded, and the cells classified as malignant by inferCNV were kept. This selection can include a few normal cells above the CNV threshold, which appear in the cluster composition below.

```{r}
load(paste0('../data/processed_data/', sample.name, '_CNV.rda'))

tumour <- subset(sobjFiltrd, subset = cnv_status == "Malignant")
ncol(tumour)
table(tumour$celltype)
```

### Neftel gene lists

Table S2 of the paper (meta-module gene lists, up to 50 genes per module, plus two cell cycle modules G1/S and G2/M).

```{r}
s2 <- read_excel("../data/reference/NIHMS1532254-supplement-9.xlsx", skip = 4)
modules <- lapply(as.list(s2), function(g) unique(na.omit(g)))
names(modules) <- gsub("/", "_", names(modules))  # G1/S -> G1_S

# Number of genes of each module measured in the data (Flex probe panel)
module_coverage <- data.frame(
  module = names(modules),
  n_genes = lengths(modules),
  n_in_data = sapply(modules, function(g) sum(g %in% rownames(tumour))))
module_coverage$pct_in_data <- round(100 * module_coverage$n_in_data / module_coverage$n_genes)
module_coverage
```

Between `r min(module_coverage$pct_in_data)` and `r max(module_coverage$pct_in_data)`% of the genes of each module are measured in the data, so the Flex probe panel covers most of every module.

### Scores

Neftel score = mean relative expression of the module genes minus the mean of a control gene set with the same expression level (30 bins, 100 control genes per gene). This is what `AddModuleScore` does. Scores are computed on the malignant cells only, as in the paper.

```{r}
modules <- lapply(modules, intersect, rownames(tumour))

tumour <- AddModuleScore(tumour, features = modules, name = "neftel_",
                         nbin = 30, ctrl = 100, seed = the.seed)

# AddModuleScore names the columns neftel_1, neftel_2... we rename them score_MES1, score_NPC1...
# (not just "NPC1" because NPC1 and NPC2 are also gene names)
score_cols <- paste0("neftel_", seq_along(modules))
names(tumour@meta.data)[match(score_cols, names(tumour@meta.data))] <- paste0("score_", names(modules))
```

### State assignment

Each cell is assigned to the meta-module with the highest score (cell cycle modules excluded), then MES1/MES2 are merged into MES-like and NPC1/NPC2 into NPC-like.

```{r}
states <- c("MES1", "MES2", "AC", "OPC", "NPC1", "NPC2")
sc <- as.matrix(tumour@meta.data[, paste0("score_", states)])

tumour$neftel_module <- states[max.col(sc, ties.method = "first")]
tumour$neftel_state <- recode(tumour$neftel_module,
                              MES1 = "MES-like", MES2 = "MES-like", AC = "AC-like",
                              OPC = "OPC-like", NPC1 = "NPC-like", NPC2 = "NPC-like")

table(tumour$neftel_state)
round(100 * prop.table(table(tumour$neftel_state)), 1)
```

### Cycling cells

As in the paper, the distribution of each cell cycle score is fitted to a normal distribution, a cell is cycling if its G1/S or G2/M score is above the P \< 0.001 threshold.

```{r}
is_high <- function(x) pnorm(x, mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x), lower.tail = FALSE) < 0.001
tumour$cycling <- is_high(tumour$score_G1_S) | is_high(tumour$score_G2_M)

table(tumour$neftel_state, tumour$cycling)
```

### Results per state

```{r}
state_summary <- tumour@meta.data %>%
  group_by(neftel_state) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            pct_tumour = round(100 * n() / ncol(tumour), 1),
            pct_cycling = round(100 * mean(cycling), 1),
            main_module = names(which.max(table(neftel_module)))) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

knitr::kable(state_summary, col.names = c("Neftel state", "n", "% of tumour cells", "% cycling", "Main module"))
```

```{r}
# Quantities used in the interpretation
pct_state <- setNames(state_summary$pct_tumour, state_summary$neftel_state)
n_state <- setNames(state_summary$n, state_summary$neftel_state)
cycling_state <- setNames(state_summary$pct_cycling, state_summary$neftel_state)

n_cycling <- sum(tumour$cycling)
pct_cycling_npc <- round(100 * sum(tumour$cycling & tumour$neftel_state == "NPC-like") / n_cycling)

n_mes1 <- sum(tumour$neftel_module == "MES1")
n_mes2 <- sum(tumour$neftel_module == "MES2")

opc_source <- sort(table(tumour$celltype[tumour$neftel_state == "OPC-like"]), decreasing = TRUE)
```

### Interpretation

-   **This tumour is dominated by MES-like (`r pct_state["MES-like"]`%) and NPC-like (`r pct_state["NPC-like"]`%) cells, with a large AC-like part (`r pct_state["AC-like"]`%)**. OPC-like cells are few (`r pct_state["OPC-like"]`%, `r n_state["OPC-like"]` cells).

-   `r n_mes1` cells were assigned to MES1 and `r n_mes2` to MES2. In the paper, MES2 is the module linked to hypoxia (its top gene is HILPDA, a hypoxia-induced gene).

-   **Cycling cells are mostly NPC-like** (`r pct_cycling_npc`% of the `r n_cycling` cycling cells). The cycling fraction is `r cycling_state["NPC-like"]`% of the NPC-like cells against `r cycling_state["MES-like"]`% of the MES-like and `r cycling_state["AC-like"]`% of the AC-like cells. This agrees with Neftel et al., where cycling is highest in the OPC-like and NPC-like states.

-   The OPC-like cells come mainly from the `r names(opc_source)[1]` population (`r opc_source[[1]]` of `r sum(opc_source)` cells). As this state is small, it is described but not interpreted quantitatively.

### Two-dimensional representation (Neftel Figure 3)

-   y-axis : D = max(OPC, NPC) - max(AC, MES), D \> 0 for OPC/NPC cells and D \< 0 for AC/MES cells

-   x-axis : log2(\|difference\| + 1) between the two states of each half, OPC and AC on the left, NPC and MES on the right

```{r}
md <- tumour@meta.data
sc_mes <- pmax(md$score_MES1, md$score_MES2)
sc_npc <- pmax(md$score_NPC1, md$score_NPC2)

md$D <- pmax(md$score_OPC, sc_npc) - pmax(md$score_AC, sc_mes)
md$x <- ifelse(md$D > 0,
               sign(sc_npc - md$score_OPC) * log2(abs(sc_npc - md$score_OPC) + 1),
               sign(sc_mes - md$score_AC) * log2(abs(sc_mes - md$score_AC) + 1))
tumour$neftel_x <- md$x
tumour$neftel_y <- md$D

quadrants <- annotate("text", x = c(-1, 1, -1, 1) * max(abs(md$x)), y = c(1, 1, -1, -1) * max(abs(md$D)),
                      label = c("OPC-like", "NPC-like", "AC-like", "MES-like"), hjust = c(0, 1, 0, 1), fontface = "bold")

ggplot(md, aes(x = x, y = D, colour = neftel_state)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  quadrants + theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Relative meta-module score", y = "D", colour = "Neftel state")

ggplot(md, aes(x = x, y = D, colour = celltype)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  quadrants + theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Relative meta-module score", y = "D", colour = "Cluster annotation")

ggplot(md[order(md$cycling), ], aes(x = x, y = D, colour = cycling)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey80", "TRUE" = "red")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  quadrants + theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Relative meta-module score", y = "D", colour = "Cycling")
```

```{r}
# Composition of each cluster in Neftel states (rows sum to 100)
cluster_state_pct <- round(100 * prop.table(table(cluster = tumour$celltype,
                                                  neftel = tumour$neftel_state), margin = 1))

# Median gap between the best and the second best module score
top2_gap <- apply(sc, 1, function(x) {
  v <- sort(x, decreasing = TRUE)
  v[1] - v[2]
})
median_gap <- round(median(top2_gap), 2)
```

### Observations on the 2D plots

-   **The NPC-like cells form a distinct group** in the top-right quadrant, which largely matches the Tumour NPC-like cluster.

-   **The AC-like and MES-like cells form a continuum** in the bottom half: there is no gap between the two states, and cells are spread from AC-like to MES-like. The Tumour MES-like cluster covers both quadrants (`r cluster_state_pct["Tumour MES-like", "MES-like"]`% MES-like and `r cluster_state_pct["Tumour MES-like", "AC-like"]`% AC-like). This fits the AC/MES plasticity described by Neftel et al.: the Neftel scores show that this cluster contains an MES-like and an AC-like component.

-   Many cells are close to the axes, i.e. between two states: the median difference between the best and the second best score is only `r median_gap`. Hybrid cells were not called, because the criteria of the paper (e.g. a score \> 1) depend on their score scale (log2(TPM/10+1)), which differs from ours.

-   The cycling cells (red) are concentrated in the NPC-like quadrant.

### Comparison with the cluster annotation

```{r}
table(cluster = tumour$celltype, neftel = tumour$neftel_state)

DimPlot(tumour, group.by = "neftel_state", label = TRUE, repel = TRUE)
FeaturePlot(tumour, features = paste0("score_", states), ncol = 3)
```

### Observations

-   Tumour NPC-like cluster: `r cluster_state_pct["Tumour NPC-like", "NPC-like"]`% NPC-like, the rest MES-like (`r cluster_state_pct["Tumour NPC-like", "MES-like"]`%) or AC-like (`r cluster_state_pct["Tumour NPC-like", "AC-like"]`%).

-   Cycling cells: `r cluster_state_pct["Cycling cells", "NPC-like"]`% NPC-like, `r cluster_state_pct["Cycling cells", "MES-like"]`% MES-like and `r cluster_state_pct["Cycling cells", "AC-like"]`% AC-like.

-   Tumour MES-like cluster: `r cluster_state_pct["Tumour MES-like", "MES-like"]`% MES-like and `r cluster_state_pct["Tumour MES-like", "AC-like"]`% AC-like; the AC-like cells are on one side of the cluster on the UMAP.

-   Hypoxic MES-like cluster: `r cluster_state_pct["Tumour MES-like (hypoxic)", "MES-like"]`% MES-like.

-   Unclear cluster: a mix of states (`r cluster_state_pct["Unclear", "MES-like"]`% MES-like, `r cluster_state_pct["Unclear", "AC-like"]`% AC-like, `r cluster_state_pct["Unclear", "NPC-like"]`% NPC-like).

-   On the UMAP, the MES1/MES2 and AC scores overlap in the same area, while NPC1/NPC2 are higher in the NPC-like cluster.

### Limits

-   The state of each cell is the module with the highest score, cells between two states are forced into one of them.

-   A single sample: the proportions describe this sample only and may depend on the dissociation (some cell states may survive it better than others). The second dissociation of the same specimen is analysed in the comparison document.

## GO enrichment of the tumour states

To see which biological processes characterise each state in this tumour, we look for the genes over-expressed in each state (vs the other malignant cells) and run a GO enrichment (Biological Process) with g:Profiler. OPC-like cells are excluded (only `r n_state["OPC-like"]` cells).

```{r}
tumour_go <- subset(tumour, subset = neftel_state != "OPC-like")
Idents(tumour_go) <- "neftel_state"

state_markers <- FindAllMarkers(tumour_go, only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25,
                                logfc.threshold = 0.5, verbose = FALSE)
state_markers <- state_markers %>% filter(p_val_adj < 0.05)

table(state_markers$cluster)
state_markers %>% group_by(cluster) %>% slice_max(avg_log2FC, n = 10) %>%
  summarise(top_genes = paste(gene, collapse = ", "))
```

The background (gene universe) is the set of genes detected in the malignant cells, not the whole genome : Flex only measures the genes of its probe panel, using the whole genome would bias the enrichment.

```{r}
detected <- rownames(tumour_go)[Matrix::rowSums(GetAssayData(tumour_go, layer = "counts") > 0) >= 10]

gene_lists <- split(state_markers$gene, state_markers$cluster)

go_states <- gost(query = gene_lists, organism = "hsapiens", sources = "GO:BP",
                  custom_bg = detected, domain_scope = "custom",
                  correction_method = "g_SCS", multi_query = FALSE)

go_res <- go_states$result
go_res %>% group_by(query) %>% slice_min(p_value, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  select(query, term_name, p_value, intersection_size, term_size)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
top_go <- go_res %>%
  filter(term_size <= 500) %>%  # remove very general terms
  group_by(query) %>% slice_min(p_value, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()

ggplot(top_go, aes(x = -log10(p_value), y = reorder(term_name, -log10(p_value)), size = intersection_size)) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ query, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "-log10(adjusted p-value)", y = NULL, size = "Genes")
```

```{r}
# Top specific GO terms per state (general terms removed), for the text
top_terms <- go_res %>%
  filter(term_size <= 500) %>%
  group_by(query) %>%
  slice_min(p_value, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  summarise(terms = paste(term_name, collapse = "; "))
top_terms_list <- setNames(top_terms$terms, top_terms$query)

# Best hypoxia-related term of the MES-like state
hypoxia_terms <- go_res %>%
  filter(query == "MES-like", grepl("hypoxi|oxygen", term_name, ignore.case = TRUE))
hypoxia_text <- if (nrow(hypoxia_terms) > 0) {
  paste0("the best hypoxia-related term had an adjusted p-value of ",
         signif(min(hypoxia_terms$p_value), 2))
} else {
  "no hypoxia-related term was significant"
}
```

### Observations

-   **MES-like**: the most specific terms were `r top_terms_list[["MES-like"]]`, and `r hypoxia_text`. The top marker genes (ADM, SERPINE1, ANGPTL4, CA12, NDRG1) are classic hypoxia-induced genes. Even if MES1 is the most frequent module, the MES-like cells of this tumour show a hypoxic programme, which fits the link between the MES state and hypoxia described by Neftel et al. They probably come from poorly oxygenated areas of the tumour (e.g. around necrosis).

-   **AC-like**: the most specific terms were `r top_terms_list[["AC-like"]]`. The markers are astrocyte genes (ATP1A2, BCAN, TTYH1, AQP1, NDRG2).

-   **NPC-like**: the most specific terms were `r top_terms_list[["NPC-like"]]`. The markers are neuronal and developmental genes (CRABP1, TAC3, CPLX1, GRIK2, MYCN, HES6).

-   Overall, the marker genes give each state a coherent biological identity: **a hypoxic MES-like compartment, an astrocytic AC-like compartment and a neurodevelopmental NPC-like compartment**.

### Limits of this enrichment

-   Partly circular : the states are defined by gene lists, so the marker genes of each state overlap these lists. GO is used to describe the states, not to prove them.

-   Cells of a single sample are not independent replicates, the p-values are inflated. The results are exploratory.

we add the states to the full object (NA for non-malignant cells) and save

```{r}
new_cols <- c(paste0("score_", names(modules)), "neftel_module", "neftel_state", "cycling", "neftel_x", "neftel_y")

neftel_meta <- tumour@meta.data[colnames(sobjFiltrd), new_cols]  # NA rows for non-malignant cells
rownames(neftel_meta) <- colnames(sobjFiltrd)
sobjFiltrd <- AddMetaData(sobjFiltrd, neftel_meta)

table(sobjFiltrd$neftel_state, useNA = "ifany")

save(sobjFiltrd, file = paste0('../data/processed_data/', sample.name, '_STATES.rda'))
```
